title: Paystride Save Interest: Daily Accrual and the Monthly Credit
content:
Paystride Save interest accrues daily and is credited once a month. The rule, stated once in full:

> Interest accrues daily on each end-of-day balance: the tier's annual percentage yield on the part up to the tier's APY balance cap, and the tier's annual percentage yield above the cap on the part above it, each converted to a daily rate over the tier's days-in-year figure, and the month's accruals are credited on the month's last calendar day, rounded to the nearest cent; a credit below the tier's smallest interest credit carries to the next month. The tier in force on each day sets that day's rates. Interest accrues while frozen when the tier pays interest while frozen, and accrued interest is forfeited on a mid-month closure when the tier forfeits uncredited interest on a mid-month closure. An account receives one interest credit per month. Interest of the tier's Form 1099-INT threshold or more in a calendar year is reported on Form 1099-INT.

## One day's interest

For each day of the month, the day's interest is the total of two parts:

1. the end-of-day balance up to the APY balance cap (that is, the lower of the end-of-day balance and the cap), multiplied by the annual percentage yield up to the cap, divided by 100 and divided by the days-in-year figure; and
2. the part of the end-of-day balance above the cap (zero when the balance does not exceed the cap), multiplied by the annual percentage yield above the cap, divided by 100 and divided by the days-in-year figure.

Each day's interest is kept unrounded. The end-of-day balance of each day is the balance as the account's entries leave it at the end of that day.

## The month's credit

The month's credit is the total of that month's daily interest amounts, rounded to the nearest cent once, on the month's last calendar day. The only rounding is of the month's total. If that credit is below the smallest interest credit, it is not credited that month and carries to the next month. An account receives one interest credit per month.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Take a hypothetical account on Paystride Save Boost all month, whose end-of-day balance is $6000.00 on each of the 30 days of a 30-day month, with Boost's figures of 2.0 percent up to a $5000.00 cap, 0.75 percent above it and 365 days in the year.

- Part up to the cap: $5000.00 multiplied by 2.0, divided by 100, divided by 365, is about $0.273973 a day.
- Part above the cap: $1000.00 multiplied by 0.75, divided by 100, divided by 365, is about $0.020548 a day.
- One day's interest: about $0.294521.
- The month: 30 days of about $0.294521 total about $8.835616, credited on the last calendar day rounded to the nearest cent as $8.84.

## Points of judgement

- **Tier change during the month.** Each day takes the rates of the tier in force on that day, so a month that spans a tier change accrues at the earlier tier's figures up to the change and at the new tier's figures after it.
- **Frozen days.** Interest accrues on frozen days when the tier pays interest while frozen.
- **Mid-month closure.** Accrued interest is forfeited when the account closes mid-month on a tier that forfeits uncredited interest on a mid-month closure.
- **Second credit for the same month.** An account receives one interest credit per month; a month that already shows an interest credit receives no other.
- **Tax reporting.** The Form 1099-INT test is the interest credited in the calendar year, compared with the tier's threshold; reaching the threshold exactly is enough.

## Tier figures this policy reads

The annual percentage yield up to the cap and the APY balance cap are tier figures: 0.5 percent up to $1000.00 on Starter, 1.25 percent up to $2500.00 on Builder, 2.0 percent up to $5000.00 on Boost, 2.75 percent up to $10000.00 on Growth, 3.3 percent up to $15000.00 on Premier and 3.8 percent up to $25000.00 on Elite.
